heroHeadline: Uganda Suspends Defence Ties With Turkey Over Somalia Troop Dispute as NISA Raid Kills Al-Shabaab Clan Commander
heroSubtitle: Uganda's military suspended all defence cooperation with Turkey on September 19, 2026, officially over Ankara's refusal to extradite a government critic, but regional sources cited by Middle East Eye and Caasimada said the real driver is friction over Uganda's roughly 6,500-strong Somalia deployment — AUSSOM's largest troop contribution, worth an estimated $60-72 million a year to Kampala — as Turkish-trained Somali forces grow more capable and Mogadishu presses Uganda to wind down its presence; the rupture adds a new fault line to AUSSOM's funding crisis a day after the US agreed to a 12-month rather than immediate UNSOS drawdown. Separately, Somalia's National Intelligence and Security Agency reported killing an Al-Shabaab clan-affairs commander, Omar Siyaad Caraaye, and three fighters in a raid near Guulane, Middle Shabelle, on September 21, wounding a second commander. AFRICOM's confirmed 2026 airstrike total held at 83+ as of September 17, and no new Al-Shabaab attacks or piracy incidents were confirmed through September 23.
